observed_scope: Exact original legacy workspace-write production token and ACL functions; owned temporary fixtures only.
observations: Ordinary outside writes are refused while full reads and authorized workspace writes succeed.
Outside/protected parent FILE_DELETE_CHILD-only opens succeed; adding FILE_WRITE_DATA is refused. Actual outside file/directory and protected .git deletion succeeds.
The partial root DELETE-only open is refused. Do not generalize that all DELETE checks bypass restricting SIDs.
inference: Fixing ACE representation and repeated repair cannot remove the independent parent deletion authorization path.
Removing FILE_DELETE_CHILD from capability allow masks is insufficient: this is already done, and the successful path remains under broad normal identity grants.
An added child capability deny alone cannot certify refusal through every parent-delete route shown by the actual native probe. No same-token/same-full-read contract repair has been established.
rejected_shortcuts: Removing WRITE_RESTRICTED or adding broad identity restricting SIDs changes the access contract.
Full-disk ACL rewrites, weakening outside-deletion tests, or changing a failed native expectation to success do not close this blocker.
A user-space wrapper or syscall hook is not an enforcement boundary for arbitrary native child processes.
A lower integrity label alone is not a proof covering outside resources at equal/lower integrity.
